ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, P is a moving point on side AD of a square $ABCD$ with side length 6 (P does not coincide with A or D). Connect $CP$, and draw $BH\perp CP$ from point B. Fold $\triangle DPC$ along the straight line containing $CP$ to obtain $\triangle CPD^{\prime}$. Extend $PD^{\prime}$ to meet the extension of $CB$ at point G. When $BH = \frac{18\sqrt{13}}{13}$, what is the length of $PG$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}

In right triangle $BCH$, $\angle BHC=90^\circ$, $BH=\frac{18\sqrt{13}}{13}$, $BC=6$,

according to the Pythagorean theorem, $CH=\sqrt{BC^2-BH^2}=\sqrt{6^2-\left(\frac{18\sqrt{13}}{13}\right)^2}=\frac{12\sqrt{13}}{13}$,

since square $ABCD$, $DC=6$,

thus $AD\parallel BC$,

therefore $\angle DPC=\angle PCB$,

therefore $\triangle PDC\sim \triangle CHB$,

therefore $\frac{PD}{CH}=\frac{DC}{HB}$,

therefore $\frac{PD}{\frac{12\sqrt{13}}{13}}=\frac{6}{\frac{18\sqrt{13}}{13}}$,

solving yields $PD=4$,

since $\triangle DPC$ is reflected along line $CP$ to get $\triangle CPD'$,

therefore $PD'=PD=4$, $D'C=DC=6$, $\angle D'PC=\angle DPC=\angle PCB$,

thus $GP=GC$,

let $GP=GC=x$, then $GD'=GP-PD'=x-4$,

in right triangle $CD'G$, $\angle CD'G=90^\circ$,

according to the Pythagorean theorem, $GC^2=GD'^2+CD'^2$,

thus $x^2=(x-4)^2+6^2$,

which gives $8x=52$,

solving yields $x=\boxed{\frac{13}{2}}$,

thus, $PG=\frac{13}{2}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a square ABCD, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right; sides AD and BC are horizontal, and AB and CD are vertical. Point P is located on the upper side AD and is not at an endpoint, and segment CP connects to P. In the figure, a segment is drawn from B to point H on CP, and a right-angle mark is used to indicate BH⊥CP. Triangle DPC is folded over along the straight line CP to obtain point D'. In the figure, D' is located on the straight line extending from P toward the lower left, and the extension of PD' intersects the leftward extension of CB at G. Reasoning: In right triangle BCH, ∠BHC=90°, BC=6, and BH=18√13/13. Therefore CH=√(BC^2-BH^2)=√(6^2-(18√13/13)^2)=√(36-4212/169)=√(1872/169)=12√13/13. Because ABCD is a square with side length 6, DC=6, and AD∥BC. Also P and D are on AD, and H, P, C are collinear, so ∠DPC=∠PCB=∠HCB; and ∠PDC=90°, ∠CHB=90°. Therefore △PDC∼△CHB. From the similarity ratio, PD/CH=DC/BH, so PD/(12√13/13)=6/(18√13/13), solving gives PD=4. Folding preserves lengths and angles unchanged, so PD'=PD=4, CD'=CD=6, and ∠PD'C=90°. Also ∠D'PC=∠DPC=∠PCB; because G is on the extension of PD', and GC is on the extension of CB, in △GPC, ∠GPC=∠GCP, therefore GP=GC. Let GP=GC=x. Since D' is on PG and PD'=4, GD'=x-4. In right triangle CD'G, CD'=6, GD'=x-4, GC=x. By the Pythagorean theorem, x^2=(x-4)^2+6^2. Expanding: x^2=x^2-8x+16+36, so 8x=52, x=13/2. Therefore PG=13/2.
